newsitem.title: QATAR: Emir opens Qatar's first LNG project and port.
newsitem.headline: Emir opens Qatar's first LNG project and port.

text.p: Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani on Monday officialy opened the Gulf state's first liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant, ushering the tiny OPEC oil producer into the league of the world's major gas exporters.

Realised at a cost of $7 billion, the Qatar Liquefied Gas Company, or Qatargas, project is designed to produce six million tonnes a year of LNG -- all committed to eight Japanese companies for 25 years from January 1997.
The project went onstream in October and delivered two shiploads of LNG to Chubu Electric Power Company in January and early this month.
Along with the plant, the Emir also officially inaugurated the 8.5 square km (3.3 square miles) Ras Laffan Port, which is billed as the world's largest LNG exporting facility.

Qatar, which possesses the world's third largest reserves of gas after Russia and Iran in its continental shelf, has planned two more LNG projects besides Qatargas to supplement its oil income -- the lowest in OPEC at under $3 billion a year.

"Qatargas establishes Qatar as a gas-exporting country and paves the way for it to play a key role in the international gas market", said Qatar's Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah.
"The implementation of a second LNG project -- Ras Laffan LNG Company -- has started and the project will commence production in mid-1999," he said.

Ras Laffan LNG Company, or Rasgas, which is designed to eventually produce 10 million tonnes a year, is 66.5 percent owned by the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) and 26.5 percent by Mobil Corp. Japan's Nissho Iwai holds four percent and Itochu three percent.
Qatar's third project is Qatar-Enron Marketing Company -- a 65-35 percent joint venture of QGPC and the U.S. Enron Corp.
Qatargas was 70 percent funded by commercial loans and export credits, arranged by international banks, and 30 percent by shareholders.
Qatargas' partners include QGPC, which owns 65 percent, Mobil and France's Total, which have a 10 percent stake each. Japan's Marubeni Corp and Mitsui Corp share the remaining 15 percent equally.
